label: prf:nsi-q-deformed-kernel
title: Proof that the $q$-deformed kernel has a hard singularity at $\hbar_q$
html:
Proof. Proof that the q-deformed kernel has a hard singularity at \hbar_q

Proof. For q \neq 1, the braiding \check{R} = \sigma \circ \mathcal{R} is non-trivial, and the categorical mass acquires a singular contribution from non-adjacent strand proximity. Concretely, because \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) depends on the q-Hodge star \star_q (Definition), the cost of two non-adjacent points \varrho(s), \varrho(t) approaching is governed by the q-deformed commutator

  [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q
  = 
  \hat{X}\hat{P} - q\hat{P}\hat{X}
  = 
  i\hbar_q,

which replaces the classical 1/r^2 repulsion kernel with the strictly stronger

  \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
   \longmapsto 
  \frac{[2]_q}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2
  - \hbar_q^{2}},

where [2]_q = q + q^{-1} is the quantum integer and \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant. This kernel has a hard singularity at \lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert = \hbar_q, creating an energy barrier of infinite height at the quantum scale. \square
